questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix. Which condition defines an $n\times m$ matrix $G$ to be a generalized inverse of $A$?
Let $A$ be a real $3\times 5$ matrix. What size must a generalized inverse $A^{I}$ of $A$ have for $AA^{I}A=A$ to make sense?
Which real matrices $A$ have at least one generalized inverse, that is, a matrix $G$ with $AGA=A$?
options: Only matrices of full row or full column rank
Only square matrices, singular or not
Every real matrix, whatever its size or rank
Only matrices that have a left or right inverse

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix with full column rank and let $L$ be a left inverse, so $LA=I_n$. Is $L$ a generalized inverse of $A$?
options: No, a generalized inverse would also need $AL=I_m$
Only if $m=n$, in which case $L$ is just $A^{-1}$
No, since for $m>n$ the left inverse $L$ is not unique

questions.question: Let $G$ be a generalized inverse of a real $m\times n$ matrix $A$, and let $\boldsymbol{b}=A\boldsymbol{x}_0$ for some $\boldsymbol{x}_0\in\mathbb{R}^n$. What can be said about $G\boldsymbol{b}$?
Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$. Which matrix $G$ is a generalized inverse of $A$, that is, satisfies $AGA=A$?

Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$, $G=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ (a generalized inverse of $A$) and $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,1)^{\top}$. What does the consistency test say about $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$?
options: $G\boldsymbol{b}=(1,0)^{\top}$, and this vector is a solution
The column-space vector $(1,2)^{\top}$ is a solution

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$, $G=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(3,6)^{\top}$. Then $I-GA=\begin{pmatrix}0&-2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. What is the set of all solutions of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$?
Let $A$ be a real $3\times 4$ matrix of rank $2$ and $G$ any generalized inverse of $A$. What is $\operatorname{rank}(GA)$?
options: It depends on which $G$ is chosen

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{a}=(1,2)^{\top}$, viewed as a $2\times1$ matrix. Which $1\times2$ row vector $\boldsymbol{g}$ is a generalized inverse of $\boldsymbol{a}$, that is, satisfies $\boldsymbol{a}\boldsymbol{g}\boldsymbol{a}=\boldsymbol{a}$?
A consistent system $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ with singular square $A$ is solved twice, using two different generalized inverses $G_1$ and $G_2$ of $A$. How do the two results compare?
options: $G_1\boldsymbol{b}=G_2\boldsymbol{b}$, since a consistent system has one solution
The two solution sets may differ, since each one depends on $G$
Only one of $G_1\boldsymbol{b}$, $G_2\boldsymbol{b}$ can solve the system
The points $G_i\boldsymbol{b}$ may differ; the solution sets agree

questions.question: Let $D=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$. Which description gives exactly the set of all generalized inverses $G=\begin{pmatrix}g_{11}&g_{12}\\g_{21}&g_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ of $D$?

Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}$, $R=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ (so $AR=I_2$) and $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,2)^{\top}$. What is the solution set of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$?
options: Only $(1,2,0)^{\top}$, since $R$ is a right inverse
A plane through $(1,2,0)^{\top}$, with one free parameter per equation

questions.question: Let $G$ be an arbitrary generalized inverse of a real matrix $A$. Which statement about $AG$ is true in general?
options: It is idempotent, but need not be symmetric
It is symmetric, while its square may differ from it
It is both symmetric and idempotent

questions.question: Let $A$ be an invertible $n\times n$ matrix and $G$ any matrix with $AGA=A$. What follows?
options: $G=A^{-1}$, so the generalized inverse is unique
$G$ may differ from $A^{-1}$ by a nonzero matrix $X$ with $AXA=O$
Nothing, since generalized inverses are never unique

questions.question: Let $O$ be the $2\times2$ zero matrix. Which $2\times2$ matrices are generalized inverses of $O$?
Let $G$ be a generalized inverse of a real $n\times n$ matrix $A$, so $AGA=A$, but with $GAG\neq G$. Which matrix $H$ is always a generalized inverse of $A$ that also satisfies $HAH=H$?
Let $A$ be a real $3\times3$ matrix of rank $2$. Which values can $\operatorname{rank}G$ take as $G$ ranges over all generalized inverses of $A$?

Let $\boldsymbol{u}=(2,1)^{\top}$, $\boldsymbol{v}=(1,2)^{\top}$ and $A=\boldsymbol{u}\boldsymbol{v}^{\top}=\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$. For which scalar $c$ is $G=cA^{\top}$ a generalized inverse of $A$?
